msg.ack.expiredForReason: The acknowledgement of {rule} for {target} expired on {date} (reason: {reason})
msg.ack.fix.declared: Acknowledge the finding again if it is still accepted, or fix it; then remove the entry from the desired state.
msg.ack.fix.ui: Acknowledge the finding again if it is still accepted, or fix it; then remove the acknowledgement under Findings.
msg.addr.cgnatWan: {inner} has the WAN address {address} from the provider's shared address space (carrier-grade NAT): nothing from the internet reaches it over IPv4.
msg.addr.cgnatWan.fix: Nothing to do if everything works. For port forwards or a VPN server over IPv4, ask the provider for a public IPv4 address, or use IPv6.
msg.addr.clientNetworks.fix: One device should be in one network. Check the port or access point it is connected to for a bridge or wrong VLAN between these networks.
msg.addr.clientOutside: {client} uses {address}, which is not in the subnet of {label} ({nets})
msg.addr.clientOutside.fix: Check for a fixed address on the client, a second DHCP server, or a port in the wrong VLAN.
msg.addr.dnsCross: Clients of {label} use {address} in {networks} as DNS server
msg.addr.dnsCross.fix: Make sure the firewall allows only DNS to that address, or hand out the router's address in {label}.
msg.addr.domainDifferent: The networks of site {site} use different domains ({detail})
msg.addr.domainDifferent.fix: Use one local domain (home.arpa recommended), or ignore this finding if the domains differ on purpose.
msg.addr.domainLocal: {segment} gets the domain {domain} from DHCP; .local is reserved for mDNS
msg.addr.domainLocal.fix: Use home.arpa (RFC 8375) or a domain you own.
msg.addr.domainMissing.fix: Set the same local domain on every network.
msg.addr.domainMissing.one: {segments} gets no domain from DHCP, while the other networks of site {site} get {domains}
msg.addr.domainMissing.other: {segments} get no domain from DHCP, while the other networks of site {site} get {domains}
msg.addr.doubleNat: {inner} gets its WAN address {address} from {outer} ({segment}, {interface}): two routers in a row{cable}.
msg.addr.doubleNat.fix: Nothing to do if everything works. If port forwards, a VPN server, games or IPv6 behind {inner} matter, put {outer} into bridge (modem) mode, or make {inner} its exposed host (DMZ) and forward the ports there.
msg.addr.duplicate.fix: Give each device its own address: change the reservation or the fixed address of one of them.
msg.addr.forwardsLost: {inner} forwards {ports} to devices behind it, but {outer} in front of it does not forward them to {inner}: from the internet these ports never arrive.
msg.addr.forwardsLost.fix: Forward the same ports on {outer} to {inner}'s WAN address, make {inner} the exposed host (DMZ) of {outer}, or put {outer} into bridge (modem) mode.
msg.addr.gateway.fix: Consider moving it to {target} (and update the DHCP router option and devices with a fixed address), or turn this rule off if the position is intended.
msg.addr.gatewayFirst: The router address of {label} is {address}, the first usable address; the other networks of this site use the last one
msg.addr.gatewayLast: The router address of {label} is {address}, the last usable address; the other networks of this site use the first one
msg.addr.gatewayMiddle: The router address of {label} is {address}, neither the first nor the last usable address of {network}
msg.addr.hostnameReserved: The host name {name} is reserved for {count} devices on {segment}: {macs}
msg.addr.hostnameReserved.fix: Rename one of the reservations, or remove the one of a device that is gone.
msg.addr.lease.fix: Use 12-24 hours (a few hours on guest networks).
msg.addr.leaseGuest: The DHCP server on {device} hands out leases of {duration} on the guest network {label}; visitors keep their address that long
msg.addr.leaseGuest.fix: Use a few hours on guest networks.
msg.addr.leaseLong: The DHCP server on {device} hands out leases of {duration} on {label}, which is very long
msg.addr.leaseShort: The DHCP server on {device} hands out leases of {duration} on {label}, which is very short
msg.addr.maskDiffers.fix: Set the mask of {name} to /{prefix} like the router's.
msg.addr.mgmtDuplicate.fix: Give every device its own address and correct the address configured in Signalbox.
msg.addr.mgmtInPool: {name} is managed at {address}, which is in the DHCP pool {pool} of {segment} without a reservation
msg.addr.mgmtInPool.fix: Add a reservation for the MAC address of {name}, or give it a fixed address outside the pool.
msg.addr.noRouter: No IPv{version} router address is known for {segment}, so the address of {names} cannot be compared with it
msg.addr.noSubnet.one: No subnet is known for {segment}, so the addresses of its {count} client cannot be checked
msg.addr.noSubnet.other: No subnet is known for {segment}, so the addresses of its {count} clients cannot be checked
msg.addr.outsideRouter: {name} has {address} on {label}, outside the router's subnet ({ref})
msg.addr.outsideRouter.fix: Set the address and mask of {name} to the router's subnet.
msg.addr.overlap.fix: Give each network its own, non-overlapping address range.
msg.addr.pool.fix: Enlarge the pool (and the subnet if needed) or shorten the lease time.
msg.addr.poolBeyond.fix: Shrink the pool to the subnet.
msg.addr.poolFull.one: The pool of {label} is full: it has {count} free address and {used} are in use
msg.addr.poolFull.other: The pool of {label} is full: it has {count} free addresses and {used} are in use
msg.addr.poolHigh.one: The pool of {label} has {count} free address and {used} are in use
msg.addr.poolHigh.other: The pool of {label} has {count} free addresses and {used} are in use
msg.addr.poolIncludes.broadcast: The pool {pool} of {label} includes {address}, the broadcast address of {network}
msg.addr.poolIncludes.fix: Start the pool after the network address and end it before the broadcast address.
msg.addr.poolIncludes.network: The pool {pool} of {label} includes {address}, the network address of {network}
msg.addr.poolIncludes.router: The pool {pool} of {label} includes {address}, the router address of {network}
msg.addr.poolOrder: The pool {pool} of {label} ends before it starts
msg.addr.poolOrder.fix: Swap the start and end address of the pool.
msg.addr.poolSeen.one: {seen} clients without a reservation have been seen on {label}, but its pool has only {count} free address
msg.addr.poolSeen.other: {seen} clients without a reservation have been seen on {label}, but its pool has only {count} free addresses
msg.addr.poolUnknown: The DHCP server on {device} for {label} did not report its pool, so its size cannot be checked
msg.addr.privateWan: {inner} has the private WAN address {address}: another router that Signalbox does not read is in front of it.
msg.addr.privateWan.fix: Nothing to do if everything works. If port forwards, a VPN server, games or IPv6 behind {inner} matter, put the router in front into bridge (modem) mode, or make {inner} its exposed host (DMZ) and forward the ports there. Add that router to Signalbox to see both.
msg.addr.recordDomain: The DNS name {name} ({address}) does not end in {domain}, the domain of {segment}
msg.addr.recordDomain.fix: Rename the record to {short}.{domain}, or use the same domain for DHCP and DNS.
msg.addr.relayed: No IPv{version} router subnet is known for {label}; the DHCP server on {device} may serve a relayed network, so its pools and reservations cannot be checked against the subnet
msg.addr.reservationIs.broadcast: The reservation {address} for {who} on {label} is the broadcast address of {network}
msg.addr.reservationIs.fix: Reserve a normal host address of the subnet for this device.
msg.addr.reservationIs.network: The reservation {address} for {who} on {label} is the network address of {network}
msg.addr.reservationIs.router: The reservation {address} for {who} on {label} is the router address of {network}
msg.addr.reservationName: The reservation for {mac} on {segment} is named {name}, the device calls itself {host}
msg.addr.reservationName.fix: Rename the reservation, or check that it is for the right device.
msg.addr.reservationOutside: The reservation {address} for {who} on {label} is outside {nets}
msg.addr.reservationOutside.fix: Reserve an address inside the subnet of the network.
msg.addr.reservedRepeated: {mac} is reserved {count} times for {address} by the DHCP server on {device} on {label}
msg.addr.reservedRepeated.fix: Remove the extra entries; they are harmless but confusing.
msg.addr.reservedTwice.fix: Keep one reservation for this device and remove the others.
msg.addr.selfAssigned.fix: Check that the DHCP server of the network is running, the pool is not full and the VLAN is carried to the port or access point.
msg.addr.selfAssigned.one: {count} client on {segment} has only a self-assigned 169.254.x.x address: {clients}
msg.addr.selfAssigned.other: {count} clients on {segment} have only a self-assigned 169.254.x.x address: {clients}
msg.addr.severalRouters.fix: Keep one router per network; put the others in access-point (bridge) mode or connect them through their own transit network.
msg.addr.wanByCable: {port} is in no network of {inner} and is cabled to {other} ({segment}): {inner} probably has its WAN there and sits behind {outer} (two routers in a row).
msg.annotations.stale.fix: If the object was renamed, move the annotation to its new id; if it is gone, remove the annotation.
msg.annotations.stale.noDevice: {target} has an annotation but belongs to no device in Signalbox (removed or disabled)
msg.annotations.stale.noSite: {target} has an annotation but belongs to a site that does not exist ({site})
msg.annotations.stale.notReportedBy: {target} has an annotation but is not reported by {device}
msg.annotations.stale.notReportedBySite: {target} has an annotation but is not reported by any device of the site
msg.annotations.stale.notSeen: {target} has an annotation but has not been seen for {days} days
msg.annotations.staleAck.fix: If the object was renamed, acknowledge the finding again; if it is gone, remove the acknowledgement.
msg.annotations.staleAck.noDevice: {target} has an acknowledgement of {rule} but belongs to no device in Signalbox (removed or disabled)
msg.annotations.staleAck.noSite: {target} has an acknowledgement of {rule} but belongs to a site that does not exist ({site})
msg.annotations.staleAck.notReportedBy: {target} has an acknowledgement of {rule} but is not reported by {device}
msg.annotations.staleAck.notReportedBySi: {target} has an acknowledgement of {rule} but is not reported by any device of the site
msg.annotations.staleAck.notSeen: {target} has an acknowledgement of {rule} but has not been seen for {days} days
msg.clients.duplicateName.fix: Rename one of them (in its own settings, not only on the router).
msg.clients.duplicateName.random: {count} devices on {where} call themselves {name} ({macs}). This may be one device that uses a private (randomised) Wi-Fi address next to its real one
msg.clients.duplicateName.random.fix: If these are different devices, rename one of them. If it is one phone or laptop, nothing is wrong; turn off its private address for this network if it should keep one name and address.
msg.clients.duplicateName.random.shared: {count} devices on networks sharing the domain {domain} ({where}) call themselves {name} ({macs}). This may be one device that uses a private (randomised) Wi-Fi address next to its real one
msg.clients.duplicateName.shared: {count} devices on networks sharing the domain {domain} ({where}) call themselves {name} ({macs})
msg.clients.iotOutside.fix: Move them to the IoT Wi-Fi or port ({target}), or change their category.
msg.clients.iotOutside.one: {count} IoT device ({clients}) is on {segment} although {target} exists
msg.clients.iotOutside.other: {count} IoT devices ({clients}) are on {segment} although {target} exists
msg.clients.randomDns: The DNS name {name} points to {address}, which a device with a randomised MAC address uses ({macs})
msg.clients.randomDns.fix: Turn off the private (random) address for this network on the device and reserve its real MAC, so that the name keeps pointing to it.
msg.clients.randomReservation: The reservation {address}{host} on {segment} is for a randomised MAC address ({mac})
msg.clients.randomReservation.fix: Turn off the private (random) address for this network on the device, then reserve its real MAC. If it is a virtual machine or container that keeps this address, nothing is wrong.
msg.clients.randomShare.fix: Nothing to fix. A device that must keep its address, name or parental controls needs its private address turned off for this network.
msg.clients.randomShare.one: {count} of {total} known clients on {segment} uses a randomised MAC address ({percent} %)
msg.clients.randomShare.other: {count} of {total} known clients on {segment} use a randomised MAC address ({percent} %)
msg.clients.userInIot.fix: Move them to the main network: the IoT network is for devices you do not trust, and they should not share it with your own.
msg.clients.userInIot.one: {count} computer, phone or server ({clients}) is in the IoT network {segment}
msg.clients.userInIot.other: {count} computers, phones or servers ({clients}) are in the IoT network {segment}
msg.clients.wrongNetwork.fix: Check the SSID it joined, or the switch port it is plugged into and that port's VLAN. If it belongs where it is now, change the expected network of the device.
msg.dhcp.fixedInPool: {address} of {device} is inside the DHCP pool {pool} on {segment}
msg.dhcp.fixedInPool.fix: Move the pool so that it starts above the fixed addresses, or give the device an address outside the pool.
msg.dhcp.multiple.fix: Keep the DHCP server on the router of this network and disable the others.
msg.dhcp.none.fix: Enable a DHCP server for this network on its router, or give every device on it a fixed address if that is intended.
msg.dhcp.poolsOverlap: DHCP server on {device} for {segment}: pools {a} and {b} overlap
msg.dhcp.poolsOverlap.fix: Shrink or merge the pools so that every address is in at most one.
msg.dhcp.reservationInPool: Reservation {address} for {who} on {segment} is inside the pool {pool}
msg.dhcp.reservationInPool.fix: Pick a reserved address outside the pool, or shrink the pool.
msg.dhcp.routerUnknown: No router address is known for {segment}, so the router option {router} of the DHCP server on {device} cannot be checked
msg.dhcp.unknown: No device at site {site} reported its DHCP servers, so it is not known whether {segments} have one
msg.dhcp.unknownDns: DHCP server on {device} tells clients on {segment} to use DNS server {servers}, which is not a known resolver or the router
msg.dhcp.unknownDns.fix: Set the DNS option to the address of your router or local DNS resolver, or turn this rule off if an outside resolver is intended.
msg.dhcp.wrongRouter: DHCP server on {device} tells clients on {segment} to use router {router}, but the router of this network is {expected}
msg.dhcp.wrongRouter.fix: Set the router (gateway) option of this DHCP server to {first}.
msg.dns.conflict.fix: Use the same record on every resolver, or use a single resolver.
msg.dns.forwarderMissing: {device} forwards DNS to {address}, but no device on {segment} uses that address
msg.dns.loop.fix: Let one of them forward to an upstream resolver (or resolve recursively) instead of to the other.
msg.dns.loopSelf: DNS lookups loop: {name} forwards to {forwarder}, itself
msg.dns.loopUnknownPort: {name} forwards DNS to {forwarder}, port {port} of {device}, where another DNS server that Signalbox does not read listens: whether lookups come back in a loop cannot be checked
msg.dns.loopUnknownService: {name} forwards DNS to {forwarder}, the DNS service {services} that Signalbox does not read: whether lookups come back in a loop cannot be checked
msg.dns.recordDynamic: The DNS record {name} points to {address}, a dynamic address of {segment} (pool {start}-{end})
msg.dns.recordDynamic.fix: Add a DHCP reservation for the device of {name} at that address, or move the record to an address outside the pool.
msg.dns.recordMismatch: The DNS record {name} points to {addresses}, the DHCP reservation for {name} is {reserved}
msg.dns.recordMismatch.fix: Update the DNS record (or the reservation) so that both use the same address.
msg.dns.recordReserved: The DNS record {name} points to {address}, which is reserved in DHCP for {reserved}
msg.dns.recordReserved.fix: Use the same name for the record and the reservation, or ignore this if the record is an intended second name.
msg.dns.recordUnknownNetwork: The DNS record {name} on {device} points to {address}, which is not in any network Signalbox knows
msg.dns.recordUnknownNetwork.fix: Correct the address (typo or an old network), or remove the record.
msg.dns.recordUnused: The DNS record {name} on {device} points to {address} on {segment}, which no known device uses
msg.dns.recordUnused.fix: Remove the record, or check the device's address.
msg.dns.resolverMissing: {device} hands out the DNS server {address}, but no device on {segment} uses that address
msg.dns.resolverMissing.fix: Update the DNS setting to an existing resolver, or bring the resolver back.
msg.dns.singleForwarder.fix: Add a second upstream resolver, or let the resolver resolve recursively.
msg.firmware.drift: {count} devices of model {model} run {versions} firmware versions ({detail})
msg.firmware.drift.fix: Update all of them to the same (newest) version.
msg.firmware.endOfLife: {name} runs firmware {current}, which is end of life
msg.firmware.endOfLife.fix: Update to a supported release, or plan to replace the device.
msg.foreign.dhcp.alert.dns: Unknown DHCP server ({who}) on {network}, handing out DNS {dns}; it reported as unknown by {seen}
msg.foreign.dhcp.alert.gw: Unknown DHCP server ({who}) on {network}, handing out gateway {gateways}; it reported as unknown by {seen}

msg.foreign.dhcp.fix.arp: Look up its address in the router's ARP table to get the MAC, then the port. Then turn off that device's DHCP server (or put it into bridge / access point mode). Typical culprits: the provider's router or a second router plugged in with its LAN side, an access point or mesh node left in router mode, a travel router, a NAS or a virtual machine host with its own DHCP server. If it is meant to be there (a second server of a failover pair Signalbox does not read), acknowledge this.
msg.foreign.dhcp.fix.mac: Find the port with that MAC address in your switches' MAC address tables (or the router's client list). Then turn off that device's DHCP server (or put it into bridge / access point mode). Typical culprits: the provider's router or a second router plugged in with its LAN side, an access point or mesh node left in router mode, a travel router, a NAS or a virtual machine host with its own DHCP server. If it is meant to be there (a second server of a failover pair Signalbox does not read), acknowledge this.
msg.foreign.dhcp.fix.ports: Its MAC address is seen on {ports}: follow that cable. Then turn off that device's DHCP server (or put it into bridge / access point mode). Typical culprits: the provider's router or a second router plugged in with its LAN side, an access point or mesh node left in router mode, a travel router, a NAS or a virtual machine host with its own DHCP server. If it is meant to be there (a second server of a failover pair Signalbox does not read), acknowledge this.

msg.foreign.dhcp.probe.none: Unknown DHCP server ({who}) on {network}; it answered {seen}

msg.foreign.ra.alert.prefix: Unknown IPv6 router ({who}) advertises on {network} (prefix {prefixes}); it reported as unknown by {seen}

msg.foreign.ra.fix.arp: Look up its address in the router's ARP table to get the MAC, then the port. Then turn off IPv6 router advertisements on that device (or its router mode), or enable RA guard on the switch port. Typical culprits: the provider's router or a second router plugged in with its LAN side, an access point or mesh node left in router mode, a travel router, a NAS or a virtual machine host with its own DHCP server. If it is a router you run on purpose, add it to Signalbox or acknowledge this.
msg.foreign.ra.fix.mac: Find the port with that MAC address in your switches' MAC address tables (or the router's client list). Then turn off IPv6 router advertisements on that device (or its router mode), or enable RA guard on the switch port. Typical culprits: the provider's router or a second router plugged in with its LAN side, an access point or mesh node left in router mode, a travel router, a NAS or a virtual machine host with its own DHCP server. If it is a router you run on purpose, add it to Signalbox or acknowledge this.
msg.foreign.ra.fix.ports: Its MAC address is seen on {ports}: follow that cable. Then turn off IPv6 router advertisements on that device (or its router mode), or enable RA guard on the switch port. Typical culprits: the provider's router or a second router plugged in with its LAN side, an access point or mesh node left in router mode, a travel router, a NAS or a virtual machine host with its own DHCP server. If it is a router you run on purpose, add it to Signalbox or acknowledge this.

msg.fritzbox.enableTr064: On the Fritz!Box, Home Network > Network > Network Settings (German: Heimnetz > Netzwerk > Netzwerkeinstellungen), switch on 'Allow access for applications' ('Zugriff für Anwendungen zulassen') and apply. Use the box's own address in the home network with the TR-064 port, normally https://<box>:49443; not the web interface port 443 and not a MyFRITZ address. The box tells its port at http://<box>:49000/tr64desc.xml if that answers.
msg.health.cpu: {name} has a CPU load of {percent}, high since {since}
msg.health.cpu.fix: Look for what keeps it busy (traffic inspection, a VPN, logging, a process that hangs); a device that is too small for the connection may need hardware offloading or a replacement.
msg.health.fan.fix: Clean or replace the fan; until then, keep the device cool.
msg.health.memory: {name} has {percent} of its memory in use
msg.health.memory.fix: Restart it, remove unused packages or features, or check for a memory leak in its firmware (an update may fix it).
msg.health.psu.fix: Check its power cable and the outlet or UPS it is plugged into; replace the power supply if it has power.
msg.health.reboot.fix: If nobody restarted it, check its power supply or PoE budget and its temperature.
msg.health.reboots: {name} restarted {count} times in the last 24 hours, last at {when}
msg.health.reboots.fix: Check its power supply or PoE budget, its temperature and its memory use; look for a firmware update if it crashes.
msg.health.rebootsReason: {name} restarted {count} times in the last 24 hours, last at {when} (reason: {reason})
msg.health.storage.fix: Remove unused packages, old logs or firmware images, or move logs to another disk. Settings and updates fail when it is full.
msg.health.temperature: {name} sensor {sensor} is at {value} °C, above the generic limit of {limit} °C
msg.health.temperature.fix: Give it more air (not in a closed cupboard, not stacked on other devices), clean its vents and check its fans.
msg.health.temperatureOwn: {name} sensor {sensor} is at {value} °C, above its limit of {limit} °C
msg.health.upsBattery.fix: Check the mains power and the UPS input cable; shut down devices that are not needed to make the battery last.
msg.health.upsNotTested.fix: Run a self-test (and schedule one, for example every three months).
msg.health.upsRuntime: UPS {ups} (on {name}) has a runtime of {minutes} minutes, less than {limit} minutes
msg.health.upsRuntime.fix: Replace the battery (they last 3 to 5 years) or move devices that do not need it to another outlet.
msg.health.upsRuntimeLoad: UPS {ups} (on {name}) has a runtime of {minutes} minutes at {load} load, less than {limit} minutes
msg.health.uptime: {name} has been running for {days} days without a restart
msg.health.uptime.fix: Check for a firmware update and install it in a quiet hour (it restarts the device); this also shows whether the device comes back up by itself.
msg.history.deviceFlapping: {name} stopped answering {count} times in the last 24 hours
msg.history.deviceFlapping.fix: Check its power supply or PoE budget, its temperature and its uplink cable.
msg.history.down.fix: Check its power and cabling, its address and password; remove it from Signalbox (or disable it) if it was replaced or retired.
msg.history.networkChanged.behind: {name} ({mac}) (now behind {device} port {port}) moved from {old} to {new} at {when}
msg.history.networkChanged.fix: If this was not intended, check the SSID it joined or the switch port it is plugged into (and that port's VLAN).
msg.history.neverAnswered: {name} has not answered since Signalbox first saw it ({since})
msg.history.portFlapping: {device} port {port} lost its link {count} times in the last 24 hours
msg.history.portFlapping.fix: Replace or re-terminate the cable, check the connectors, and leave both ends on auto-negotiation.
msg.history.portFlapping.to: {device} port {port} (to {peer}) lost its link {count} times in the last 24 hours
msg.history.staleReservation: The reservation {address}{host} on {segment} is for {mac}, which has not been seen for more than {days} days
msg.history.staleReservation.fix: Remove the reservation if the device is gone. A device that is rarely on (a camera in the garden in winter) keeps it; turn the rule off if needed.
msg.ipv6.none.fix: Add a /64 from the delegated prefix to this network, or turn this rule off if IPv6 is disabled there on purpose.
msg.ipv6.prefixLength.fix: Use a /64 per network; split a larger delegated prefix into /64s.
msg.ipv6.ulaOnly.fix: Add a /64 from the delegated prefix to this network, or turn this rule off if it should stay local on purpose.
msg.ipv6.ulaOnly.one: {segment} has only a local (ULA) IPv6 prefix while {names} has a global one
msg.ipv6.ulaOnly.other: {segment} has only a local (ULA) IPv6 prefix while {names} have a global one
msg.ipv6.unchecked: Clients on {segment} have IPv6 addresses, but no router at the site reported IPv6 subnets, so it is not known whether a router announces them
msg.ipv6.unknownPrefix.fix: Look for another router, hotspot or virtual machine host on this network that sends router advertisements, and turn them off there.
msg.ipv6.unknownPrefix.one: {count} client on {label} uses addresses from {prefix}, which no router of {label} announces
msg.ipv6.unknownPrefix.other: {count} clients on {label} use addresses from {prefix}, which no router of {label} announces
msg.leases.declined: The DHCP server on {device} marked {addresses} on {segment} as declined: another device already uses it
msg.leases.declined.fix: Find the device that uses the address and move it outside the pool (or give it a reservation), then clear the declined lease.
msg.leases.option121: The DHCP server on {device} hands out classless static routes on {segment} without a default route, so clients ignore the router option and have no way out
msg.leases.option121.fix: Add a route 0.0.0.0/0 to the classless routes, or remove them.
msg.leases.option121.via: Add a route 0.0.0.0/0 via {router} to the classless routes, or remove them.
msg.leases.relayNoServer: The DHCP relay on {where} for {segment} has no server to forward to
msg.leases.relayNoServer.fix: Enter the address of your DHCP server in the relay settings.
msg.leases.relayNoServerEnabled: The DHCP relay on {where} for {segment} forwards to {target}, but no DHCP server is enabled on {names}
msg.leases.relayNoServerEnabled.fix: Enable the DHCP server there, or point the relay to the right address.
msg.leases.relayTargetUnknown: The DHCP relay on {where} for {segment} forwards to {target}, which is not a device Signalbox knows, so it cannot tell whether a DHCP server runs there
msg.leases.relayTargetUnread: The DHCP relay on {where} for {segment} forwards to {target}, but the DHCP servers of that device could not be read
msg.leases.staticInPool: {name} ({mac}) uses {addresses} inside the DHCP pool of {segment} without a lease
msg.leases.staticInPool.fix: Give {name} a reservation, or a fixed address outside the pool. If the address is meant to be fixed, mark the device as using a static address.
msg.mac.flapping: {who} moved {count} times in the last 24 hours between {ports} ports, among them {names}; now behind {port}
msg.mac.flapping.fix: Look for a loop in the cabling (two cables between the same switches, a switch plugged into itself) and turn on spanning tree; check that no two devices use the same MAC address and that a bonded or virtual NIC is set up consistently.
msg.mac.stale.fix: Remove the entry if the device is gone. A device that is rarely on keeps it; mark it as may be unreachable or turn the rule off.
msg.mac.staleFor: The static MAC address table entry for {mac} on {where} is for a device not seen for more than {days} days
msg.mac.staleSince: The static MAC address table entry for {mac} on {where} is for a device not seen since {date}
msg.mac.tableFull: {device} has {count} entries in its MAC address table (Signalbox keeps at most {limit}); the topology it shows may be incomplete
msg.mac.tableFull.fix: Check for a loop or a device flooding random addresses; on a large network the devices behind a full table are placed by their other sightings only.
msg.mgmt.insecure.fix: On {name}: turn off what is not needed, or restrict it to a management network; use SSH or HTTPS instead of plain text, SNMPv3 instead of a community and SSH keys only for root.
msg.mgmt.insecureLimited: {name} has {what} enabled, limited to some networks or addresses
msg.mgmt.offered.fix: Offer the services only in the LAN or a management VLAN on {name}, or block {segment} from reaching them.
msg.mgmt.offeredUnknown: {name} has an address in {segment} and offers {services} on it; its firewall does not decide it exactly ({reasons}), so it is not known whether they are blocked from there
msg.mgmt.offeredUnknownNoFirewall: {name} has an address in {segment} and offers {services} on it; without its firewall rules (not read) it is not known whether they are blocked from there
msg.mgmt.plaintext.both: Signalbox sends the password of {name} unencrypted in {segment} (clients: {clients}, Wi-Fi networks: {ssids})
msg.mgmt.plaintext.clients: Signalbox sends the password of {name} unencrypted in {segment} (clients: {clients})
msg.mgmt.plaintext.fix: Move the management of the device to a separate VLAN without clients or Wi-Fi, so nobody else can capture the password.
msg.mgmt.plaintext.ssids: Signalbox sends the password of {name} unencrypted in {segment} (Wi-Fi networks: {ssids})
msg.mgmt.wanExposed.fix: Turn off remote access to {name} (or restrict it to your VPN) and use a VPN for administration from outside.
msg.mgmt.wanUnknown: {name} offers {services} on its internet connection; its firewall does not decide it exactly ({reasons}), so it is not known whether they are blocked from the internet
msg.mgmt.wanUnknownNoFirewall: {name} offers {services} on its internet connection; without its firewall rules (not read) it is not known whether they are blocked from the internet
msg.networks.addressIn.fix: Remove the address (a switch or access point only needs to forward that VLAN), or block access from that network to it.
msg.networks.guestNoIsolation: The guest Wi-Fi {ssid} on {aps} lets its clients reach each other
msg.networks.guestNoIsolation.fix: Turn on client isolation for the SSID (desired state: client_isolation: true; OpenWrt: option isolate '1').
msg.networks.guestNoIsolation.guessed: The guest Wi-Fi {ssid} (guessed from its name) on {aps} lets its clients reach each other
msg.networks.guestShared.fix: Bind it to a separate guest VLAN (or the router's guest network).
msg.networks.guestShared.guessedFix: Bind it to a separate guest VLAN (or the router's guest network). If the guess is wrong, declare the purpose in the desired state (purpose: main on the SSID or segment).
msg.networks.guestShared.others: The guest Wi-Fi {ssid} on {aps} is in {segment}, the same network as {others}
msg.networks.guestShared.others.guessed: The guest Wi-Fi {ssid} (guessed from its name) on {aps} is in {segment}, the same network as {others}
msg.networks.guestShared.purpose: The guest Wi-Fi {ssid} on {aps} is in {segment}, which is {network}
msg.networks.guestShared.purpose.guessed: The guest Wi-Fi {ssid} (guessed from its name) on {aps} is in {segment}, which is {network}
msg.networks.guestShared.untagged: The guest Wi-Fi {ssid} on {aps} is in {segment}, the untagged main network
msg.networks.guestShared.untagged.guesse: The guest Wi-Fi {ssid} (guessed from its name) on {aps} is in {segment}, the untagged main network
msg.networks.iot5ghz: The IoT SSID {ssid} at site {site} is only on {bands} GHz
msg.networks.iot5ghz.fix: Also broadcast it on 2.4 GHz, unless all its devices support 5 GHz.
msg.networks.managedIn.fix: Move its management address to the LAN or a management VLAN, or block access from {segment} to it.
msg.networks.purposeMissing: It is not declared what these networks at site {site} are for: {networks}
msg.networks.purposeMissing.fix: Declare them in the desired state, e.g. segments: [{vlan: 20, purpose: iot}] (main, guest, iot, management, servers, lab, voice, cameras, transit, other).
msg.networks.reachable.fix: Block {segment} from reaching {name} in the firewall of its router, or move {name} to a management VLAN that {segment} cannot reach.
msg.networks.reachable.via: {services} of {name} ({address}) can be reached from {network} through the firewall of {who}
msg.networks.routerUnknown: {name} is reachable at {addresses} in {network}; without firewall rules it is not known whether its management interface is blocked from there
msg.ports.adminDown: {name} is disabled, but {far} is connected to it.
msg.ports.adminDown.fix: Enable the port, or move the cable to an enabled port (and remove a link you entered by hand if the cable is gone).
msg.ports.autoneg: {fixed} is set to {forced}, the connected port {auto} uses auto-negotiation.
msg.ports.autoneg.fix: Set both ports to auto-negotiation (or, only if a device requires it, the same fixed speed and duplex on both).
msg.ports.clientVlan.fix: Check the VLAN of the port and the network settings of the device (a fixed address, VLAN tagging on the device, or a switch in between).
msg.ports.clientVlanAccess: {who} is on {port} ({segment}, access port) but uses {address} in {clientSegment}.
msg.ports.clientVlanPvid: {who} is on {port} ({segment}, PVID) but uses {address} in {clientSegment}.
msg.ports.description: The description of {name} names {named}, but {connected} is connected to it.
msg.ports.description.fix: Update the port description, or check whether the cable is in the right port.
msg.ports.eee: Energy-efficient Ethernet is on for {names} (link {a} to {b}).
msg.ports.eee.fix: Turn off energy-efficient Ethernet (EEE, green Ethernet) on {names}.
msg.ports.mtu.fix: Use the same MTU on both ends ({standard} unless every device on the path supports jumbo frames).
msg.ports.pvidMismatch: {name} sends {segment} untagged, but its PVID puts incoming untagged frames into {pvid}.
msg.ports.pvidMismatch.fix: Set the PVID of {name} to the VLAN of {segment}, or make that VLAN tagged on the port.
msg.ports.severalUntagged.fix: Keep one untagged VLAN on the port (set the PVID to the same one) and make the others tagged.
msg.read.fix.authFailed: Check the user name and password or API key of the device.
msg.read.fix.unreachable: Check that the device is on and its address is right.
msg.read.fix.untrusted: Compare the fingerprint with the device and trust it if it matches.
msg.read.untrusted: {name} presented a certificate that is not trusted: {error}
msg.setup.linux.createUser: Create the user {login} (no password, no sudo, no groups)
msg.setup.linux.deleteUser: Delete the user {login} and its home directory
msg.setup.linux.hostKey: Trust the device's SSH host key for reading (the one confirmed for this setup)
msg.setup.linux.key: Let {login} log in with a new key generated by Signalbox (only the public key is sent; authorized_keys is replaced)
msg.setup.linux.noSudoers: No sudoers rule: neither WireGuard (wg) nor nftables (nft) is installed
msg.setup.linux.previewHostKey: Trust the SSH host key you confirmed, for reading
msg.setup.linux.previewInstall: Install nftables with the device's package manager
msg.setup.linux.previewInstallIproute2: Install iproute2 (ip -j, bridge) with the device's package manager
msg.setup.linux.previewInstallTracepath: Install tracepath with the device's package manager
msg.setup.linux.previewInstallWireguard: Install wireguard-tools with the device's package manager
msg.setup.linux.previewKey: Authorize a new SSH key for it (public key only)
msg.setup.linux.previewSudoers: Allow it the read-only wg show and nft list commands
msg.setup.linux.previewUser: Create the user signalbox (no password, no sudo)
msg.setup.linux.sudoers: Allow {login} the read-only commands (wg show, nft list ruleset) ({path})

msg.time.dhcpMismatch.unused: {device} hands out the NTP server {address} on {segment}, but no device on {where} uses that address
msg.time.noLocal.none: No device at {site} serves time: {names} ask the internet
msg.time.noLocal.noneFix: Turn on the NTP server of {gateway} and point the devices (and DHCP option 42) to {address}.
msg.time.noLocal.served: {names} use only internet NTP servers, although {servers} serves time at {site}
msg.time.noServer.fix: Turn on its NTP client with a server.
msg.time.noServer.fixHint: Turn on its NTP client with a server (for example {servers}).
msg.time.notSynchronised: {name} is not synchronised with its NTP servers ({servers})
msg.time.notSynchronised.fix: Check that the servers are right and reachable from the device (firewall, DNS for names); use the gateway if it serves time.
msg.time.offset.fix: Configure NTP on it and check that it can reach the NTP server.
msg.time.offset.fixHint: Configure NTP on it ({servers} can serve time) and check that it can reach the NTP server.
msg.time.timezone.fix: Set the same time zone on every device of the site.
msg.time.unreachable.fix: Point it to a device that serves time, or turn on the NTP server of that device for this network.
msg.time.unreachable.off: {device} uses the NTP server {address}, but {name} does not serve time
msg.time.unreachable.offHere: {device} uses the NTP server {address}, but {name} does not serve time on {where}
msg.time.unreachable.unused: {device} uses the NTP server {address}, but no device on {where} uses that address
msg.topology.duplicate.fix: Remove all but one of them from Signalbox (keep the one read through the controller if it is managed by one).
msg.topology.hidden: {count} devices are seen behind {port}, which has no known neighbour.
msg.topology.hidden.fix: If a switch or access point is connected there, add it under Devices or enter it on the Topology page.
msg.topology.hidden.taggedFix: If a switch or access point is connected there, add it under Devices or enter it on the Topology page. An unmanaged switch should not be on a port with tagged VLANs.
msg.topology.hiddenNets: {count} devices in {networks} networks are seen behind {port}, which has no known neighbour.
msg.topology.lagAuto.fix: Set all members to auto-negotiation and check their cables.
msg.topology.lagDevices.fix: Connect all members of the LAG to one device (or one switch stack).
msg.topology.lagDuplex: {label}: some members run in half duplex.
msg.topology.lagDuplex.fix: Set all members to auto-negotiation and full duplex.
msg.topology.lagFarMixed: {label} is connected to {ports}, which are not all in the same LAG.

msg.topology.lagFarNoLag: {label} is connected to {ports}, which are not in a LAG.

msg.topology.lagFarUnknown: {device} does not report its ports, so the far end of {label} could not be checked.
msg.topology.lagSingle.fix: Check the cables and the far end of the members that are down.
msg.topology.lagSpeeds: {label}: the members run at different speeds ({speeds}).
msg.topology.lagVlans.fix: Configure the VLANs on the LAG itself, or the same VLANs on every member.
msg.topology.mgmtShared.both.one: {names} is managed in {segment}, which also has clients: {clients}; SSIDs: {ssids}.
msg.topology.mgmtShared.both.other: {names} are managed in {segment}, which also has clients: {clients}; SSIDs: {ssids}.
msg.topology.mgmtShared.clients.one: {names} is managed in {segment}, which also has clients: {clients}.
msg.topology.mgmtShared.clients.other: {names} are managed in {segment}, which also has clients: {clients}.
msg.topology.mgmtShared.fix: Move the management addresses to {management}, the management network.
msg.topology.mgmtShared.fixNone: Consider a management VLAN that only admin devices can reach, and move the management addresses there.
msg.topology.mgmtShared.ssids.one: {names} is managed in {segment}, which also has SSIDs: {ssids}.
msg.topology.mgmtShared.ssids.other: {names} are managed in {segment}, which also has SSIDs: {ssids}.
msg.topology.spof: Single points of failure towards {gateway} (what is cut off): {points}.
msg.topology.spof.fix: Consider a second uplink (with LAG or spanning tree) for these devices, or keep a spare.
msg.topology.unknownNeighbour.fix: If it is a router, switch or access point, add it under Devices. Phones and computers that send LLDP can be ignored.
msg.topology.unknownNeighbour.one: {ports} sees a device announcing itself as {who} that is not in Signalbox.
msg.topology.unknownNeighbour.other: {ports} see a device announcing itself as {who} that is not in Signalbox.
msg.trace.extraNat: {source} reaches the internet through {count} router(s) with private addresses, Signalbox expects {expected}
msg.trace.extraNat.fix: Find the router at that address: put an ISP box into bridge or exposed-host mode, or add the router to Signalbox; acknowledge this if the provider numbers its routers privately.
msg.trace.extraNat.unknown: {source} reaches the internet through {count} router(s) with private addresses, Signalbox expects {expected} (unknown: {unknown})
msg.trace.notViaTunnel: {source} reaches {target} through {where} first, not through the tunnel {tunnel} that routes it
msg.trace.notViaTunnel.fix: Check the route to that network on the device (it should point into the tunnel) and whether the tunnel is up; trace again afterwards.
msg.transport.http401.fix: Check the user name and password (or API key and secret) in the settings.
msg.transport.http403: {path}: access denied (HTTP 403); check the user's privileges
msg.transport.http403.fix: The login works but may not read this. Give the user the privileges the setup guide of this integration lists (the link is in the device settings).
msg.transport.http404: {path}: not found (HTTP 404); is the API enabled?
msg.transport.http404.fix: Check that the address points to the device itself (with the right port and path) and that its API is enabled; some parts need an extra package.
msg.transport.reach.fix: Check that the device is on, that the address and port in the settings are right, and that Signalbox can reach it (same network or routed, no firewall in between).
msg.transport.sshAuth.fix: Check the user name and password, and that the device allows a password login over SSH for it.
msg.transport.sshDeniedAdmin: {where}: the device refused the admin login over SSH
msg.transport.sshFailed: cannot open an SSH connection to {where}: {reason}
msg.transport.tlsFailed: cannot open a TLS connection to {where}: {reason}
msg.vlan.belowMax: The link {link} runs at {speed} Mbit/s, but both ports support {max} Mbit/s.
msg.vlan.belowMax.fix: Use a cable rated for the higher speed (Cat 5e or better for 2.5 Gbit/s, Cat 6a for 10 Gbit/s), check that both ports advertise it in auto-negotiation, and replace a damaged cable.
msg.vlan.duplex.fix: Set both ports to auto-negotiation (or the same fixed speed and duplex).
msg.vlan.halfDuplex: The link {link} runs in half duplex on {ports}.
msg.vlan.halfDuplex.fix: Set both ports to auto-negotiation (or the same fixed speed and full duplex); if it stays, replace the cable.
msg.vlan.missing: {segment}, used on {users}, is not carried on the link {link} (missing on {ports}).
msg.vlan.missingMac: {segment}, used on {users}, is not configured on {ports}. The link {link} is only inferred from a MAC table and may run through devices that are not read, so this could not be checked. Enable LLDP on both devices or enter the cable by hand.
msg.vlan.native.fix: Set the same untagged (native) VLAN on both ports, or none on both.
msg.vlan.nativeMac: {link}: {a_port} sends {a} untagged, {b_port} sends {b} untagged. It is only inferred from a MAC table and may run through devices that are not read, so this could not be checked. Enable LLDP on both devices or enter the cable by hand.
msg.vlan.noMemberships: {device} does not report VLAN memberships, so {link} could not be checked.
msg.vlan.portHalfDuplex.fix: Set the port and the connected device to auto-negotiation; if it stays, replace the cable.
msg.vlan.portSlow.fix: Check the cable and the connected device; almost every device today reaches at least 100 Mbit/s.
msg.vlan.slowLink.fix: Replace the cable (it may use only two pairs) or check that both ports are set to auto-negotiation.
msg.vlan.speed.fix: Set both ports to auto-negotiation; if it stays, replace the cable.
msg.vlan.tagged: {segment} is tagged on {here} but not configured on {there} ({link}).
msg.vlan.tagged.fix: Add {segment} as tagged VLAN to {there}, or remove it from {here}.
msg.vlan.taggedMac: {segment} is tagged on {here} but not configured on {there} ({link}). The link is only inferred from a MAC table and may run through devices that are not read, so this could not be checked. Enable LLDP on both devices or enter the cable by hand.
msg.vlan.trunkScope: The link to {ap} carries {names}, but {ap} only uses {uses}.
msg.vlan.unconnected: {name} is not connected to the gateway in the known topology, so the path of its VLANs could not be checked. Add the missing link (cable or wireless uplink) or enable LLDP on the devices in between.
msg.vlan.unread: {device} was not fully read, so {link} could not be checked.
msg.vlan.unused: {segment} has a subnet on {names} but no other port and no SSID uses it.
msg.vlan.unused.fix: Remove the VLAN and its subnet if it is no longer needed, or add it to the ports and SSIDs that should use it.
msg.vpn.handshake.fix: Check that the other end is running and reachable (its public address or name, the port, the firewall in front of it) and that both ends have the other's public key.
msg.vpn.handshake.idleFix: Check that the other end is running and reachable (its public address or name, the port, the firewall in front of it) and that both ends have the other's public key. Without a persistent keepalive an idle tunnel stays quiet by design.
msg.vpn.handshakeNever: On tunnel {tunnel}, peer {peer} has not completed a handshake since the tunnel came up
msg.vpn.handshakeStale: On tunnel {tunnel}, peer {peer} has not completed a handshake for {minutes} minutes
msg.vpn.keepaliveNat: Tunnel {tunnel} is behind NAT and has no persistent keepalive for peer {peer}: the tunnel stops working when it is idle
msg.vpn.keepaliveNat.fix: Set the persistent keepalive of the peer to 25 seconds.
msg.vpn.localOverlap: On tunnel {tunnel}, peer {peer} routes {network}, which overlaps the local network {local}: the two cannot be told apart
msg.vpn.localOverlap.fix: Use different address ranges at the two ends (a VPN between two sites with the same network cannot route), or narrow the allowed IPs of the peer.
msg.vpn.noSuchNetwork: On tunnel {tunnel}, peer {peer} ({other}) is sent {network}, but no network like it exists at the other end
msg.vpn.noSuchNetwork.fix: Correct the allowed IPs of the peer to the networks that really lie behind the other end, or add the network there.
msg.vpn.notListed: On tunnel {tunnel}, peer {peer} is tunnel {other}, but that tunnel does not list {tunnel} as a peer
msg.vpn.notListed.fix: Add the public key of this tunnel as a peer on the other end (with the networks of this site as its allowed IPs), or remove the peer here.
msg.vpn.overlap: On tunnel {tunnel}, peer {a} and peer {b} both route {network}: only one of them gets that traffic
msg.vpn.overlap.fix: Give each peer its own networks in its allowed IPs; remove the network from the peer that should not carry it.
msg.vpn.unrouted: On tunnel {tunnel}, peer {peer} accepts {network}, but the device has no route for it through the tunnel
msg.vpn.unrouted.fix: Let the device add the routes of the allowed IPs (OpenWrt: route allowed IPs on the peer) or add a static route for the network through the tunnel interface. A route set by a script is not seen: acknowledge the finding then.
msg.wan.cgnat: The internet connection {label} is behind carrier-grade NAT: connections from the internet over IPv4 cannot reach the site
msg.wan.cgnat.fix: Ask the provider for a public IPv4 address (or IPv6), or use a VPN or tunnel service that connects outwards.
msg.wan.cgnat.fixIpv6: Reach the devices at home over IPv6 (open the port for IPv6 in the firewall), or ask the provider for a public IPv4 address.
msg.wan.dnsMismatch: {device} forwards DNS to {forwarder} on the network of the internet connection {label}, but the provider hands out {servers}
msg.wan.dnsMismatch.fix: Forward to the DNS servers the provider hands out ({servers}), or to a resolver you chose, instead of the old address.
msg.wan.down.fix: Check the cable and the modem, the account details if it logs in (PPPoE), and whether the provider reports an outage.
msg.wan.downWorking: The internet connection {label} is down; the internet works through {working}
msg.wan.downWorking.fix: Check the cable or modem of this line, and the account details if it logs in (PPPoE). Turn the rule off for this line if it is a standby line.
msg.wan.dslite: The internet connection {label} is behind DS-Lite (IPv4 through the provider's carrier-grade NAT): connections from the internet over IPv4 cannot reach the site
msg.wan.noIpv6: The internet connection {label} has a delegated IPv6 prefix ({prefixes}), but no network with clients has IPv6 from it
msg.wan.noIpv6.fix: Give each client network a /64 from the delegated prefix (router advertisements on), or turn this rule off if IPv6 stays off on purpose.
msg.wan.noIpv6Unknown: The internet connection {label} has a delegated IPv6 prefix ({prefixes}), but {device} reported no IPv6 on its networks, so it is not known whether they use it
msg.wifi.channelPlan.fixEu: Use channel 1, 6 or 11 (or 1, 5, 9 and 13 on all access points).
msg.wifi.coverageAps: SSID {ssid} is broadcast by {have} but not by {missing}
msg.wifi.coverageAps.fix: Add {ssid} to {missing}, or ignore this if it is meant to cover only part of the site.
msg.wifi.coverageBand: SSID {ssid} is on {band} GHz at {with} but not at {lacking}, although they have a {band} GHz radio
msg.wifi.coverageBand.fix: Add {ssid} to the {band} GHz radio of {lacking}, or ignore this if it is intended.
msg.wifi.defaultSsid.fix: Set up the access point (own SSID name and password) or turn the radio off.
msg.wifi.defaultSsidOpen: {device} broadcasts the factory SSID {ssid} without a password (open)
msg.wifi.dfs.fix: If clients lose Wi-Fi now and then, try channels 36-48 or 149-165.
msg.wifi.dfsReach: Radio {radio} uses channel {channel} at {width} MHz, which reaches the DFS channels {first}-{last}
msg.wifi.hidden.fix: Hiding adds no security; consider broadcasting it and relying on WPA2/WPA3.
msg.wifi.passphraseReuse.fix: Give each network its own passphrase, or put the SSIDs into one network.
msg.wifi.passphraseReuse.guestFix: Give the guest network its own passphrase.
msg.wifi.passwordsDiffer: SSIDs {names} use different passwords but put clients into the same network {segment}
msg.wifi.passwordsDiffer.fix: If the SSIDs should be separated (IoT, guests), give each its own network (VLAN); otherwise ignore this or turn the rule off.
msg.wifi.pmfDisabled: SSID {ssid} on {ap} uses WPA2/WPA3 with protected management frames (PMF) disabled, so every client stays on WPA2
msg.wifi.pmfDisabled.fix: Set protected management frames (PMF, 802.11w) to optional.
msg.wifi.pmfNotRequired: SSID {ssid} on {ap} uses {mode} with protected management frames (PMF) {pmf}
msg.wifi.pmfNotRequired.fix: Set protected management frames (PMF, 802.11w) to required.
msg.wifi.pmfUnknown: {ap} did not report the protected management frames (PMF) setting of SSID {ssid}, so it is not known whether it matches {mode}
msg.wifi.sixGhzH2e: SSID {ssid} on the 6 GHz radio of {device} derives the WPA3 password only with hunting-and-pecking, which 6 GHz clients do not accept
msg.wifi.sixGhzH2e.fix: Set the SAE password element (sae_pwe) to hash-to-element (H2E).
msg.wifi.sixGhzSecurity: SSID {ssid} on radio {radio} uses {mode}, which 6 GHz does not allow
msg.wifi.sixGhzSecurity.fix: On 6 GHz use WPA3 only (or OWE for an open network) with protected management frames required. Keep WPA2/WPA3 transition mode on 2.4 and 5 GHz if old devices need it.
msg.wifi.ssidCount: Radio {radio} broadcasts {count} SSIDs ({names}); more than {max} cost noticeable airtime
msg.wifi.ssidCount.fix: Merge SSIDs or turn off the ones you do not need (each one costs airtime).
msg.wifi.txAps: On {band} GHz at site {site}, {loud} sends at {loud_dbm} dBm and {quiet} at {quiet_dbm} dBm
msg.wifi.txAps.fix: Bring the access points within about 6 dB of each other, usually by lowering the loud one.
msg.wifi.txBands: The 2.4 GHz radio of {device} sends at {low} dBm, its 5 GHz radio at {high} dBm
msg.wifi.txBands.fix: Lower 2.4 GHz to about 3-6 dB below 5 GHz so that clients prefer 5 GHz.
msg.wifi.weakSecurity.openFix: Use WPA2/WPA3 with AES (CCMP) only, or OWE (Enhanced Open) for a guest network.
msg.wifi.weakestLink.fix: Move {ssid} to its own network (VLAN), for example a guest network.
msg.wifi.weakestUnknown: It is not known which network (VLAN) the unprotected SSIDs {ssids} at site {site} use, so it is not known whether they share one with a protected SSID
msg.wifi.widthWide: Radio {radio} uses {width} MHz at a site with {count} {band} GHz access points
msg.wifi.widthWide.fix5: Use 80 MHz so that the access points can use channels that do not overlap.
msg.wifi.widthWide.fix6: Use 160 MHz or less so that the access points can use channels that do not overlap.
msg.wifi.wpa3Available: SSID {ssid} on {device} uses WPA2 only although the radio supports WPA3
msg.wifi.wpa3Available.fix: Switch to WPA2/WPA3 transition mode (protected management frames optional).
msg.wifi.wps: WPS is turned on for SSID {ssid} on {device}
msg.wifi.wps.button: WPS (push button) is turned on for SSID {ssid} on {device}
msg.wifi.wps.fix: Turn WPS off; join devices with the passphrase or a QR code instead.
msg.wifi.wps.pin: WPS (PIN) is turned on for SSID {ssid} on {device}
msg.wireless.countries: Radios at site {site} use different country codes ({parts})
msg.wireless.countries.fix: Set the same country code, the one of the country the site is in, on every radio.
msg.wireless.differs.client_isolation: SSID {ssid} at site {site}: client isolation differs ({parts})
msg.wireless.differs.client_isolation.fi: Set the same client isolation for {ssid} on every access point.
msg.wireless.differs.hidden: SSID {ssid} at site {site}: hidden setting differs ({parts})
msg.wireless.differs.hidden.fix: Set the same hidden setting for {ssid} on every access point.
msg.wireless.differs.passphrase_fingerpr: Set the same passphrase for {ssid} on every access point.
msg.wireless.differs.pmf: SSID {ssid} at site {site}: protected management frames (PMF) differs ({parts})
msg.wireless.differs.pmf.fix: Set the same protected management frames (PMF) for {ssid} on every access point.
msg.wireless.differs.roaming_80211k: SSID {ssid} at site {site}: neighbour reports (802.11k) differs ({parts})
msg.wireless.differs.roaming_80211k.fix: Set the same neighbour reports (802.11k) for {ssid} on every access point.
msg.wireless.differs.roaming_80211r: SSID {ssid} at site {site}: fast roaming (802.11r) differs ({parts})
msg.wireless.differs.roaming_80211r.fix: Set the same fast roaming (802.11r) for {ssid} on every access point.
msg.wireless.differs.roaming_80211v: SSID {ssid} at site {site}: BSS transition (802.11v) differs ({parts})
msg.wireless.differs.roaming_80211v.fix: Set the same BSS transition (802.11v) for {ssid} on every access point.
msg.wireless.differs.security: SSID {ssid} at site {site}: security mode differs ({parts})
msg.wireless.differs.security.fix: Set the same security mode for {ssid} on every access point.
msg.wireless.differs.segment_id.fix: Set the same network (VLAN) for {ssid} on every access point.
msg.wireless.noCountry: {radio} has no country code set (or did not report it)
msg.wireless.noCountry.fix: Set the country code of this radio to the country it is used in.
msg.wireless.noSubnet: SSID {ssid} on {device} uses {segment}, which has no subnet on the router
msg.wireless.noSubnet.fix: Create this VLAN with an address and DHCP on the router, or bind the SSID to a network that exists there.
msg.wireless.noSubnetUnknown: No router at site {site} reported its subnets, so it is not known whether the networks of {ssids} exist there
msg.wireless.overlap.fix: Move one of the access points to a channel that does not overlap, or use a narrower width.
msg.wireless.overlap.fix24: Move one of the access points to a channel that does not overlap (1, 6 or 11).
net.noneKnownHint: Signalbox shows {what} once a device that reports them has been read.
probes.off: Probes are off: this lists only servers the devices report (their own leases, rogue DHCP alerts). With probes.enabled: true Signalbox's host also asks every network it is attached to who answers DHCP and router solicitations.
probes.on: Signalbox's host sends one DHCPDISCOVER (never a request: no lease is taken) and one IPv6 router solicitation on each network it is attached to. Servers that are no device Signalbox knows are findings.
probes.title: DHCP servers and routers answering
rule.ack.expired.explanation: An acknowledgement of a finding has passed its end date, so the finding counts as a problem again if it still exists. Renew the acknowledgement or remove it.
rule.ack.expired.title: Acknowledgement expired
rule.addr.duplicate-ip.explanation: The same IP address belongs to devices with different MAC addresses (seen as clients or set as DHCP reservations). Only one of them can work at a time.
rule.addr.duplicate-ip.title: Address used by more than one device
rule.addr.subnet-overlap.explanation: Two different networks (VLANs, or networks at different sites) use overlapping address ranges. Routers cannot tell where to send traffic for those addresses, so some devices become unreachable.
rule.addr.subnet-overlap.title: Subnets overlap
rule.dhcp.dns-option.explanation: The DNS servers a DHCP server tells its clients should be the resolver of this network (a DNS service Signalbox knows, or the router). Clients that use another resolver bypass local names, filtering and ad blocking, or fail if that address does not exist.
rule.dhcp.dns-option.title: DHCP hands out an unknown DNS server
rule.dhcp.one-server.explanation: Every network (VLAN) with a router needs exactly one DHCP server that hands out addresses. With none, devices that join the network get no address; with two, they answer each other's clients with different addresses, gateways or DNS servers and connections break at random.
rule.dhcp.one-server.title: One DHCP server per network
rule.dhcp.pool-fixed-address.explanation: An address that a router, switch or access point uses on this network lies inside the range the DHCP server hands out. Sooner or later a client gets the same address and both stop working.
rule.dhcp.pool-fixed-address.title: Router or device address inside a DHCP pool
rule.dhcp.pools-overlap.explanation: Two address pools of the same DHCP server cover the same addresses. The server may hand out one address twice or refuse to start.
rule.dhcp.pools-overlap.title: DHCP pools overlap
rule.dhcp.reservation-in-pool.explanatio: A static reservation uses an address from the dynamic pool. Many DHCP servers can hand that address to another client while the reserved device is offline; keeping reservations outside the pool avoids the conflict.
rule.dhcp.reservation-in-pool.title: Reserved address inside a DHCP pool
rule.dhcp.router-option.explanation: The router (default gateway) a DHCP server tells its clients must be the address of the router on that network. Otherwise clients can reach their neighbours but not the internet.
rule.dhcp.router-option.title: DHCP hands out the wrong router
rule.signalbox.read.explanation: A device did not answer, refused the login, presented an untrusted certificate, or one of its capabilities failed. Checks that need this data are incomplete until it is fixed.
rule.signalbox.read.title: Device could not be read completely

setup.preview.remove: Signalbox would remove what it set up. Usually:
